properties.natural_language: Any incoming P2P block data request must contain valid block numbers that can be parsed as unsigned integers.
Block data requests targeting block numbers below 15,537,393 (Paris upgrade) must be rejected by eth/70 clients.
GetBlockBodies (0x05) messages must have their block number scope validated before processing.
GetReceipts (0x0f) messages must have their block number scope validated before processing.
After block number check completes for a post-PoS request (>= 15,537,393), the requested block data must be served to the peer.
After block number check determines pre-PoS data (< 15,537,393), the request must be rejected and no data returned.
An eth/70 client must never serve block bodies or receipts for blocks below 15,537,393.
During the protocol transition, the mixed network state must support both eth/69 and eth/70 clients coexisting without data loss for post-PoS blocks.
The rejection mechanism for pre-PoS data requests must be defined (silent drop or explicit error).
Block 15,537,393 must be treated as the immutable boundary between pre-PoS and post-PoS data across all eth/70 message types.
After protocol upgrade completes, the client must operate under eth/70 rules and refuse pre-PoS data queries.
After message scope validation determines block >= 15,537,393, the message must be accepted as within scope.
After message scope validation determines block < 15,537,393, the message must be marked out of scope.
BlockBodies (0x06) and Receipts (0x10) response messages must be scope-validated before processing.
Alternative data retrieval mechanisms (archive nodes, Era files) must be available for pre-PoS historical data.
Light clients relying on post-PoS data must not require pre-PoS historical verification for security guarantees.
The trusted checkpoint root provided for light client bootstrap must originate from a verified weak subjectivity source.
LightClientUpdate objects received from full nodes must contain valid sync committee signatures with at least 2/3 supermajority.
Light client P2P bootstrap requests must be sent to authenticated peers and responses cryptographically verified.
After successful bootstrap, the light client store must contain a valid finalized header and the current sync committee.
After processing a valid LightClientUpdate, the finalized header must advance to a slot >= the previous finalized header slot.
After processing an optimistic update, the light client's optimistic head slot must be >= the finalized header slot.
The light client's finalized header slot must never decrease across any update operation.
At least 2/3 of the sync committee members must be honest for light client updates to be trustworthy.
The light client must maintain connectivity to at least one honest full node to prevent eclipse attacks.
After fork epoch detection, the light client store must be upgraded to the new fork's data structures.
Fork version-specific data structure changes must be defined by the individual fork specs.
After subscribing to gossip topics, the light client must begin receiving updates via GossipSub.
After requesting updates by range, the light client must receive updates covering the specified sync committee periods.
Before eth_requestAccounts can return account addresses, explicit user consent must be obtained via an isolated approval dialog.
The Ethereum provider (window.ethereum) must be verified as available before any account request can proceed.
The caller context and origin must be validated before processing eth_requestAccounts RPC calls.
After user approval, the resolved promise must contain an Array of at least one valid Ethereum address string.
After user rejection, the promise must be rejected with an informative Error object.
Account addresses must never be exposed to a DApp without prior explicit user consent via the approval dialog.
The consent dialog must accurately display the requesting origin and be isolated from DApp JavaScript manipulation.
Repeated requests after user rejection should be handled gracefully without spamming the user.
Error objects returned on rejection must contain at minimum a message property.
After checking existing permission and finding a cached grant, accounts may be returned without re-prompting the user.
When no cached permission exists, the full consent flow must be initiated.
When no Ethereum provider is detected, the DApp must be informed that no provider is available.
DApp must check provider existence before calling eth_requestAccounts.
Invalid or empty response arrays must be caught and treated as errors.
No-accounts-available and provider error conditions must generate appropriate error objects.
Request failure must be properly classified into user rejection, no accounts, or provider error.
The RPC request from the DApp must be received and validated before processing.
Blocks received from peers must have their block number validated to determine the active gas cost ruleset.
Transactions crafted with many IO-heavy operations must be metered using the correct gas schedule for the block's fork.
After fork activation at block 2,463,000, all IO-heavy operations must use EIP-150 repriced gas costs.
After gas deduction with new costs, insufficient gas must result in an out-of-gas exception.
After the fork is deployed, the same DoS attack pattern must become economically infeasible.
For blocks below 2,463,000, the pre-Tangerine Whistle gas costs must be used; for blocks at or above, EIP-150 costs must apply.
IO operation gas costs must accurately reflect the true computational cost to prevent denial-of-service attacks.
No alternative underpriced operations should exist that allow similar DoS effects after the fork.
IO-heavy operations include SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, and SELFDESTRUCT.
After gas lookup under old rules, the pre-Tangerine costs must be applied.
After gas lookup under new rules, the EIP-150 repriced costs must be applied.
DoS attack via cheap IO operations must cause network degradation pre-fork.
Blocks received from peers must have their claimed difficulty validated against the computed expected difficulty using EIP-649 rules.
After Byzantium activation, difficulty must be computed using fake_block = max(0, block_number - 3,000,000) for the ice age component.
After difficulty computation completes, the ice age component must equal 2^(fake_block // 100000 - 2).
After Byzantium activation, block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (3e18 wei) instead of 5 ETH.
Uncle inclusion rewards must be computed as (8-k) * 3 ETH / 8 for uncle miners and 3 ETH / 32 for the nephew miner.
After difficulty comparison, blocks with difficulty != expected must be rejected as invalid.
After difficulty comparison, blocks with difficulty == expected must be accepted as valid.
The difficulty bomb delay of 3,000,000 blocks must be consistently applied to all post-Byzantium blocks.
The reduced block reward (3 ETH) must maintain sufficient mining incentive for network security.
All client implementations must compute difficulty and rewards identically for consensus.
The BYZANTIUM_FORK_BLKNUM must be correctly configured per network (4,370,000 for mainnet).
Pre-Byzantium blocks must use the 5 ETH reward and original difficulty without bomb delay.
Parent block difficulty and timestamp must be available for difficulty computation.
Block miner must produce a valid block for reward computation.
The page origin must be verified as a secure context (window.isSecureContext === true) before provider injection.
The origin must meet W3C Secure Contexts trustworthiness criteria (HTTPS, localhost, file://) before provider injection.
Iframe contexts must have their first-party vs third-party status determined before provider access decisions.
After all security checks pass for a trustworthy origin, window.ethereum must be injected and available.
After detecting an insecure context, window.ethereum must remain undefined (provider blocked).
After determining an untrustworthy origin, the provider must be blocked.
Third-party iframes must be blocked from provider access by default.
The browser must correctly implement and report window.isSecureContext for provider security to function.
HTTPS origins must have valid certificate chains to trusted root CAs.
First-party iframes with compatible sandbox settings must be allowed provider access.
First-party iframes with restrictive sandbox must be blocked from provider access.
Third-party iframes with explicit Permissions API grant must be allowed provider access.
HTTP localhost with developer mode enabled must be granted provider access.
HTTP localhost with developer mode disabled must be blocked from provider access.
Developer mode must default to disabled to minimize attack surface.
Attackers must not be able to compromise the localhost development environment when dev mode is enabled.
Sandbox attributes on first-party iframes must be checked for allow-same-origin compatibility.
Third-party iframe provider access requires explicit permission via Permissions API.
BLS-to-execution-change gossip messages must be validated for current_epoch >= CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH.
Each BLS-to-execution-change must be the first valid change received for the given validator index.
Beacon block gossip messages must have their fork digest verified against the expected Capella fork digest.
Block request/response must determine the correct fork version for serialization based on the block's epoch.
After all BLS-to-execution-change validation passes, the message must be accepted and forwarded to peers.
After BLS-to-execution-change validation fails, the message must be rejected.
After pre-Capella epoch detection, the BLS change message must be ignored.
After duplicate detection, the BLS change message must be ignored.
After fork version determination, blocks must be serialized in the correct fork-specific format.
After fork digest verification fails, the beacon block must be rejected.
After fork digest and content validation pass, the block must be accepted for processing.
Wall-clock time used for epoch calculation must be reasonably synchronized across nodes.
An attacker must not be able to forge valid BLS signatures for bls_to_execution_change messages.
Peers must correctly implement fork-versioned serialization and deserialization.
Epoch threshold check must pass before proceeding to validator-index uniqueness check.
The size parameter for byte padding operations must be a valid non-negative integer.
The size parameter must be bounded to prevent memory exhaustion from extremely large values.
After left padding, the result must have zero bytes prepended to reach the target size.
After right padding, the result must have zero bytes appended to reach the target size.
When value length >= target size, the original value must be returned unmodified (no truncation).
After padding execution, memory must be allocated for the padded result.
Byte padding operations must preserve the original data content and only add zero bytes.
Callers must provide semantically correct size values for the byte data being processed.
Sufficient memory must be available for the padded result to prevent allocation failures.
After size conversion, the integer value must be ready for use in padding operations.
Block signing requests from the beacon node must be validated against the slashing protection database before signing.
The validator must be completely stopped before importing slashing protection interchange files.
Interchange files from external clients must pass full validation: JSON schema, genesis root match, BLS key validity.
The genesis_validators_root in the interchange file must match the current network configuration.
Block slot must be >= minimum previously signed slot before signing is approved.
Attestation source epoch must be >= minimum previously signed source epoch.
Attestation target epoch must be >= minimum previously signed target epoch.
After block signing approval and signing, the signed block must be recorded in the slashing protection database.
After attestation signing approval and signing, the signed attestation must be recorded in the slashing protection database.
After genesis root mismatch, the import must be rejected.
After successful genesis root validation and record merge, the slashing DB must be updated.
A validator must never sign two different blocks for the same slot (no double proposals).
A validator must never create surround votes (no attestation A surrounds or is surrounded by attestation B).
Missing signing roots in interchange files must be treated as potential conflicts for maximum safety.
An attacker must not be able to trigger file import while the validator is actively signing.
After JSON schema validation passes, proceed to BLS key validation.
After JSON schema validation fails, the import must be rejected.
After BLS key validation and signing root verification, data becomes trusted for import.
After block slot is below floor, signing must be rejected.
After epoch is below floor, attestation signing must be rejected.
After all block checks pass, signing must be approved.
After all attestation checks pass, signing must be approved.
Attestation signing requests must include source epoch, target epoch, and attestation data.
Interchange file must be parsed before genesis root validation.
Duplicate public keys in interchange files must be safely merged.
All DApp requests via provider.request() must contain a valid method field in the RequestArguments.
Potentially malicious DApp requests must be sanitized and rate-limited before processing.
Network connectivity events must carry verified chainId in hex format.
After successful wallet processing, the promise must resolve with the RPC method result.
After wallet error, the promise must reject with a ProviderRpcError containing code and message.
After validation failure, the request must be rejected with appropriate error.
After rate limit exceeded, the request must be rejected.
After connection established, a 'connect' event must be emitted with chainId.
After all connections lost, a 'disconnect' event must be emitted with ProviderRpcError.
After chain switch, a 'chainChanged' event must be emitted with the new chainId.
After user authorizes accounts, the accounts must be exposed and accountsChanged emitted.
After user revokes accounts, accounts must no longer be exposed.
The Provider must never contain private user data - all private data must remain in the Wallet.
Provider-Wallet isolation must be maintained at all times during request processing.
The Provider object at window.ethereum must not be modifiable by DApp JavaScript after injection.
Error codes must follow the standardized values: 4001 (user rejected), 4100 (unauthorized), 4200 (unsupported), 4900 (disconnected), 4901 (chain disconnected).
After security checks pass, request must be securely forwarded to Wallet.
After validation passes, request must be routed to wallet.
Event listeners should be properly cleaned up when DApps unmount.
